C
An infinite sum, or series, is defined as the sum of an infinite sequence of numbers, meaning it has an unlimited number of terms that are added together.

B
A convergent series is defined by its sequence of partial sums approaching a specific, finite value. In contrast, the partial sums of a divergent series do not approach a finite value; they might grow to infinity, decrease to negative infinity, or oscillate.

B
The concept of convergence relies on terms or partial sums getting arbitrarily close to each other and to a limit. The standard way to measure the distance between two real numbers, x and y, is by taking the absolute value of their difference, |x - y|, which is the absolute value metric.

B
In the 2-adic metric, the distance between two numbers, x and y, is determined by the highest power of 2 that divides their difference (x - y). The higher the power of 2 that divides their difference, the smaller the 2-adic distance is, and therefore the "closer" the two numbers are.

C
In the 2-adic metric, numbers with high powers of 2 are considered "small". The terms of the series (1, 2, 4, 8, ...) get progressively smaller and approach zero, causing the series to converge. The sum can be calculated using the geometric series formula: Sum = a / (1 - r) = 1 / (1 - 2) = -1.
